messages.author: b998e9d6a5be0399
messages.subject: Adding Higher-Order Function to Stan's Grammar
parts:
Hello,

and thank you in advance for your help.

I originally posted this on the users mailing list (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/integrate_ode$20function_signatures/stan-users/qJDiAks_HrE/W-RplDMdAQAJ). Bob redirected me here. I am honored to be on the Stan development list :)

I am trying to add a higher-order function to Stan, for applications in Pharmacometrics. The function, GeneralCptModel_CVODE, is written in C++, and takes advantage of a library I wrote in Stan-compatible C++. I cannot add the function using "add()" in the function_signatures file because one of my function's argument is a function.

Following the example of integrate_ode_cvode(), I modified several grammar files, but could not build CmdStan successfully. These are the errors the compiler returns:

stan/lib/stan_math/lib/boost_1.58.0/boost/fusion/container/vector/convert.hpp:25:30: error: implicit instantiation of undefined template 'boost::fusion::detail::barrier::as_vector<13>'

stan/lib/stan_math/lib/boost_1.58.0/boost/fusion/container/vector/convert.hpp:26:26: error: 'apply' following the 'template' keyword does not refer to a template template apply<typename result_of::begin<Sequence>::type>::type

In between there is a lot of text, which is pretty hard to interpret. I figured the error lied in term_grammar_def.hpp, particularly the following lines of code:

GeneralCptModel_CVODE_r
%= (lit("GeneralCptModel_CVODE") >> no_skip[!char_("a-zA-Z0-9_")])
> lit('(')
> identifier_r // system function name (function only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // pMatrix
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // time
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // amt
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // rate
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // ii
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // evid (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // cmt (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // addl (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // ss (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // rel_tol (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // abs_tol (data only)
> lit(',')
> expression_g(_r1) // max_num_steps (data only)
> lit(')') [validate_GeneralCptModel_CVODE_f(
_val, boost::phoenix::ref(var_map_),
_pass, boost::phoenix::ref(error_msgs_))];


It looks as if there are too many arguments (13 here). If I delete the last three "expression_g(_r1)" statements, CmdStan builds correctly. This leads me to think there is a 10 arguments limit for functions directly added to Stan's grammar. Is this a constrain I need to work with, or is there a way around it?

I posted all the modified grammar files on GitHub. The name of the branch is charlesm93:CompartmentModelGrammar.

~ Charles

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Higher-Order Function to Stan's Grammar
parts:
Now I see what's going on (despite my mailer deciding those << are
two layers of replies).

That's not a limit in Stan per se, but it may be coming from
Boost's Spirit Qi parser.

I think you should be able to get around this by replacing

a << b << c << d

with

(a << b) << (c << d).

It should work for longer expressions, too.

If that doesn't work, then it'll need to be broken up into
smaller rules, e.g., with a new grammar rule e

a << b << e;

defined by

e %= c << d;

- Bob

parts:
Any idea where the limit of 10 is coming from? When
they say "expression" in the error message, it's not
about expressions in the Stan syntax, but C++ expressions.

Just replacing one element isn't going to help.

What you can do is create something like a control object,
which would be a relative tolerance, absolute tolerance,
and max number of steps. It would require the AST piece
(.hpp and _def.cpp) and it would require a new rule (.hpp
and _def.hpp), but it would reduce the number of right-hand
side expressions by two. Then you can write the rule with
a Fusion adapter and %=.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Higher-Order Function to Stan's Grammar
parts:
I am not sure what might cause the limit. My guess is that one of the functions used in boost is overloaded to have between 0 and 10 arguments. This is the case for the ADD function used in function_signatures.h, which can have up to 7 arguments (for potentially interested viewers, the way around this limit is to use a vector of arguments, which only counts as one argument. It seems we are trying to do the same here, with the grammar rule being equivalent to a vector.)

The compiler does not explicitly state there is a 10 arguments limit. The error message is :

stan/lib/stan_math/lib/boost_1.58.0/boost/fusion/container/vector/convert.hpp:25:30: error:
implicit instantiation of undefined template
'boost::fusion::detail::barrier::as_vector<13>'

typedef typename gen::
^

where I have tried to create a function with 13 arguments. Note the as_vector<13> becomes as_vector<n> if I use n arguments. When n <= 10, this error no longer appears. This led me to think there was a 10 arguments limit.

The full error message is pasted at the end of this post.

I'll create an additional argument object (with 4 arguments), but I am unsure if this approach will work, given using integrate_ode_cvode_r in lieu of expression_g(_r1) did not work. -- there is of course only one way to find out!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Higher-Order Function to Stan's Grammar
parts:
Thanks --- that makes it clearer where the issue
is --- boost::fusion is the wrapper that converts
sequences into generic lists for template programming
and I'm pretty sure your diagnosis is spot on.

Either way, it's easy to work around with new intermediate
rules.

- Bob

> On Mar 14, 2016, at 9:57 AM, Charles Margossian <charles.ma...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I am not sure what might cause the limit. My guess is that one of the functions used in boost is overloaded to have between 0 and 10 arguments. This is the case for the ADD function used in function_signatures.h, which can have up to 7 arguments (for potentially interested viewers, the way around this limit is to use a vector of arguments, which only counts as one argument. It seems we are trying to do the same here, with the grammar rule being equivalent to a vector.)
>
> The compiler does not explicitly state there is a 10 arguments limit. The error message is :
>
> stan/lib/stan_math/lib/boost_1.58.0/boost/fusion/container/vector/convert.hpp:25:30: error:
> implicit instantiation of undefined template
> 'boost::fusion::detail::barrier::as_vector<13>'
> typedef typename gen::
> ^
>
> where I have tried to create a function with 13 arguments. Note the as_vector<13> becomes as_vector<n> if I use n arguments. When n <= 10, this error no longer appears. This led me to think there was a 10 arguments limit.
>
> The full error message is pasted at the end of this post.
>
> I'll create an additional argument object (with 4 arguments), but I am unsure if this approach will work, given using integrate_ode_cvode_r in lieu of expression_g(_r1) did not work. -- there is of course only one way to find out!
